toegepas.voor: Ys smelt tot water en kookwater
toegepas.na: Ys smelt tot water, en kookwater
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS comma: 'en' joins two main clauses, each with its own subject and verb.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining two main clauses ('Ys smelt' / 'kookwater word').
toegepas.rede_keurder: Both clauses have their own subject and verb, so the AWS 2017 requires the comma; meaning unchanged.

toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS comma: 'en' joins an imperative main clause to a clause with its own subject 'dit' and verb.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining an imperative clause to a clause with its own subject 'dit'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Two full clauses joined by 'en' take the comma, and it matches change 9 for consistency.

toegepas.rede_vinder: A three-item list reads more naturally with a comma than with a repeated 'of'.
toegepas.fout: The repeated 'of' in 'nat of koud of hard' reads clumsily.
toegepas.rede_keurder: A comma list is the natural form; under the negation it still says the particle is none of the three.

toegepas.voor: Daar kom geen deeltjies by nie en geen
toegepas.na: Daar kom geen deeltjies by nie, en geen
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS comma: 'en' joins two main clauses, each with its own subject and verb.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' between two negated main clauses.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Each clause has its own subject and verb ('kom ... by' / 'verdwyn'), so the comma is required; meaning unchanged.

toegepas.voor: Vaste plekke geld dus vir elke vaste stof.
toegepas.na: Elke vaste stof se deeltjies het dus vaste plekke.
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Vaste plekke geld vir' is abstract and wooden; saying whose places they are is clearer and keeps the meaning.
toegepas.fout: 'Vaste plekke geld dus vir elke vaste stof' is abstract and wooden.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The proposal says the same thing plainly, echoes the glass sentence before it, and touches no protected wording.

toegepas.voor: 'n vaste plek nie en hulle sit
toegepas.na: 'n vaste plek nie, en hulle sit
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS comma: 'en' joins two main clauses with different subjects ('geeneen' and 'hulle').
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining clauses with different subjects ('geeneen' / 'hulle').
toegepas.rede_keurder: Two full clauses joined by 'en' take the comma; the protected wording is untouched.

toegepas.na: In albei toestande is die deeltjies
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'albei' has no noun to refer to inside this block; naming the states makes the reference clear.
toegepas.fout: Bare 'albei' has no noun to point to at the start of the sentence.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'albei toestande' makes the reference clear for a Grade 6 reader without changing the claim.

toegepas.na: teen mekaar of teen die wande
toegepas.rede_vinder: Repeating the preposition makes clear that the particles bump against the walls, not into 'each other or the walls' as one object.
toegepas.fout: The preposition is not repeated after 'of', so 'die wande' hangs loosely.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Repeating 'teen' is the careful Afrikaans form and keeps the same meaning: particles bump into each other or into the walls.

toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS comma: 'en' joins an imperative main clause to a clause with its own subject 'die deeltjies' and verb; matches the parallel sentence in the second block.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining an imperative clause to a clause with subject 'die deeltjies'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Two full clauses take the comma, consistent with change 2.

toegepas.voor: vinnig genoeg beweeg by die oppervlak
toegepas.na: vinnig genoeg beweeg, by die oppervlak
toegepas.rede_vinder: A comma closing the relative clause separates the colliding verbs and stops 'beweeg by' being read as one verb.
toegepas.fout: Without a comma the verbs 'beweeg' and 'ontsnap' collide and 'beweeg by die oppervlak' can be misread.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Closing the relative clause with a comma removes the stumble and keeps the meaning that fast particles escape at the surface.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The noun 'afkoeling' is the standard form as a sentence subject; a bare infinitive as subject reads colloquially.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: An infinitive as subject is normal Afrikaans, so 'Afkoel werk andersom' already reads well and the noun form is a lateral move.
